applied_by: tools/dictionary/pipeline/publish_corpus.py --notebook-collation; the published corpus reproduces from the restoration checkpoint, the v2 receipt and this file
note_on_supersession: The six revert records below supersede v2 corrections that remain in provenance/v2-effective-diff.json. That receipt is a record of what commit dc186a2 did and is left intact; the corpus moves on. Each record here names the v2 correction it reverts, and test_site.py checks the last correction touching a field rather than assuming there is only one. The three t039 line 76 records added in the second round supersede v2 corrections in the same way, but only two of them restore a documentary value; the English field held no English in the documentary record either, and its record says so explicitly.
note_on_line_divisions: Records with change_kind repair-line-division move Miluk words between two adjacent published lines so that each line matches the English printed beside it. They add, drop and alter nothing: check 7 holds the pair to the same words it held documentarily. They do change the 1990 line division, which the project otherwise leaves alone, so each is directed by Troy and the documentary division is kept in each line's documentary_original_fields.
note_on_multiple_records_per_field: A field may carry more than one record here when a later pass builds on an earlier one -- t039 line 76 is first reverted to its documentary value and then redivided. Records apply in file order, and anything checking that a correction took effect must look at the last record touching that field, not every one.
